description: nf-core/oncoanalyser samplesheet context, aligned to the pinned 3.0.0 schema. Whole-genome tumour/normal DNA from FASTQ through the Hartwig WiGiTS tools: somatic SNVs, indels, SVs, copy number, purity and ploidy, drivers, HLA, signatures, HRD, tissue of origin and the ORANGE report.

mode.help: Whole genome (and transcriptome) mode. The pipeline sets no default and stops without one. targeted mode is not offered: it needs a panel's resource files (only TSO500 on GRCh37 is built in), and purity_estimate, panel_resource_creation and prepare_reference are not analyses of these samples.

processes_exclude.help: comma list of processes to skip, from lib/Constants.groovy Process: alignment, amber, bamtools, chord, cider, cobalt, cuppa, esvee, isofox, lilac, linx, multiqc, neo, orange, pave, peach, purple, qsee, redux, sage, sage_append, sage_visualiser, sigs, teal, virusinterpreter, wisp. Skipping an upstream process silently skips everything that needs it (the pipeline raises no error), so skip only report or annotation steps, e.g. virusinterpreter,orange.

pipeline.name: nf-core/oncoanalyser
pipeline.core_rule: Long format, one row per FASTQ pair: group_id (the patient; the analysis unit and output folder), subject_id (the same value as group_id), sample_id (the D.SEQ UID), sample_type tumor or normal, sequence_type dna, filetype fastq, info library_id:<id>;lane:<lane>, and filepath <R1>;<R2>. Each group holds exactly one tumour DNA sample and one normal DNA sample here.

validation_rules: No cell may contain a space (assets/schema_input.json pattern ^\S+$), a comma, or a semicolon other than the ones below.
filetype is fastq on every row; filepath is read 1 and read 2, gzipped, joined by one ';' (exactly two paths: lib/Utils.groovy refuses any other count). Single-end or interleaved FASTQ cannot run.
info holds library_id:<id>;lane:<lane> on every FASTQ row (both keys are required). library_id + lane (+ flowcell when given) must differ between the rows of one sample.
sample_type is tumor or normal, from the param atlas verdict; never guess it from a name alone. A swapped tumour and normal gives a plausible, wrong somatic analysis.

Each group_id holds one tumour DNA sample_id and one normal DNA sample_id, and subject_id is the same on every row of a group. A group with only a normal stops the run; this launch also refuses a tumour with no normal.
sequence_type is dna. RNA libraries are not part of this launch.
Only whole-genome libraries (LibraryStrategy WGS). Exome or panel data in wgts mode gives wrong copy number and purity; targeted mode needs custom panel resources that are not built.

BAM or CRAM leaves (GDC/TCGA alignments) are not accepted: oncoanalyser needs alignments to its own bundled GRCh38_hmf genome with soft-clipped supplementary reads and mate CIGARs (usage.md, Sequencing technologies).
notes: Reference data: --genome GRCh38_hmf. Every genome file (FASTA, index, dict, BWA-MEM2 index, GRIDSS index) and the WiGiTS resource bundle default to URLs under data.oncoanalyser.com, which oncoanalyser downloads into the work directory on every run unless ref_data_genome_* and ref_data_hmf_data_path name local copies (usage.md, Staging reference data). That bundle is not staged on the cluster, so the launcher must pass those paths from a staged GRCh38_hmf bundle, and configure_run refuses oncoanalyser until one is registered. Nothing here downloads it.

samplesheet_columns.description: Column-level field dictionary for the nf-core/oncoanalyser input samplesheet (FASTQ rows).

group_id.description: Groups a tumour and its normal into one analysis; names the output folder.
group_id.validation_hints: The UID of the PAT sample in the leaf's lineage, as sarek's patient. Never invent a shared id to make a pair.

subject_id.description: Patient id; must be the same within a group.

sample_id.description: Sample id; output file prefix (tumour id for most files).
sample_id.validation_hints: The NExtSEEK D.SEQ UID, repeated on every FASTQ row of that sample.

sample_type.validation_hints: From the param atlas verdict; asked of the user when the metadata does not decide it.

sequence_type.description: DNA libraries only in this launch.

info.description: Library and lane of this FASTQ pair.
info.validation_hints: library_id = the D.SEQ UID; lane = the L00N token of the file name without the L, else 001, 002 in file order.

filepath.description: Read 1 and read 2 of one pair, ';'-separated.
filepath.validation_hints: Absolute cluster paths from the sample's Link_PrimaryData / File_PrimaryData.

report_writer_guidance.purpose: Build an nf-core/oncoanalyser samplesheet from a resolved NExtSEEK D.SEQ cohort of whole-genome tumour and matched-normal DNA libraries.
report_writer_guidance.workflow_role: Selected for a whole cancer-genome analysis (somatic SNV/indel, SV, copy number, purity/ploidy, drivers, report) of WGS tumour/normal pairs. For germline calls, exomes or a run that can go now use sarek; for a panel of normals use createpanelrefs.
population_priority: One row per FASTQ pair; sample_id = the D.SEQ UID; group_id = subject_id = the PAT UID in the lineage.
sample_type from the param atlas verdict (tumor or normal); ask where it is conflict or absent.
Say plainly that the Hartwig GRCh38_hmf reference bundle is not staged on the cluster, so the run cannot be submitted yet, and that nothing is downloaded.
final_checks: Every group has one tumor and one normal sample_id, sequence_type dna.
Every filepath holds exactly two .fastq.gz paths joined by ';'; every info holds library_id and lane, unique per sample.

runtime.basis: First guess for one 16-CPU Luria node; not measured. oncoanalyser documents no runtimes; whole-genome tumour/normal from FASTQ (alignment, REDUX, GRIDSS-index-backed SV calling) is expected to take far longer than sarek germline calling.
